REPORT OF IBE COMMI'ITEE ON PUBLIC SCHOOLS
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.&: A .M. of California:
Your Grand Lodge Public Schools Committee is pleased to report a very successful series of activities for 1988 culminating in many outstanding Public Schools Week
programs during April. We received reports from the Worshipful Masters of 227
Lodges which represents nearly 40% of the Lodges in the jurisdiction. The report form,
requested annually, was redesigned for 1988 into a simpler one page report which
allowed for any amount of additional comments. Many such useful comments were
included by the reporting Masters. Over 25% of the Lodges used materials which our
Committee made available at cost or less. These materials included pamphlets, posters,
pencils, certificates of appreciation, and book covers. Similar materials are to be
offered for 1989 with rulers being added to the list of items.
Under the leadership of Committeeman Darci Reynolds, our Little Red Schoolhouse pin was introduced. This little pin has become very popular and approximately
4,000 have been distributed far and wide. They will continue to be available as long as
the demand exists.
Our Committee took advantage of the opportunity to participate in the 1988
Masonic Leadership Workshops. In each, we made presentations in the prepared
program as well as having a table display of our materials and services.
One of our objectives each year is to contact each Lodge urging their participation
in Public Schools Week activities with an explanation of the Lodges' responsibilities
and of the services that our Committee is prepared to offer to assist each Lodge. These
contacts are made by individual Committeemen primarily by participating, with the
permission of the lnspector, at District Officers Meetings. Unfortunately, the distribution of our Committeemen has not made it possible for us to contact many Districts in
outlying areas of the jurisdiction. Recognizing this, Grand Master Leo B. Mark filled
existing vacancies so that in 1988 we were able to contact more Lodges. Deputy Grand
Master Stanley L. Channon is preparing to continue making Committee appointments
in areas of need.
Grand Master Mark appointed the Chairman of this Committee to serve on the
Task Force for the Drug and Alcohol Abuse Program. In this, it is planned that the
Public Schools Committee will have a major role to play. It is expected that the thrust
of Public Schools Week will be directed to programs to fight drug and alcohol abuse
in our Public Schools.
Finally, the Public Schools Committee extends its appreciation and thanks to the
Grand Lodge Officers and staff who have counseled and assisted us in our efforts. We
anticipate their continued support in the future.

REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE
ON LODGE RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A..M. of California:
The Masonic Lodge Resources Development Committee is pleased to present the
following Annual Report and recommendations for the 1987-88 Masonic year.

There are 15 Committee members presently serving on the Resources Committee.
Three other Brethren provide consulting assistance as requested.
We meet with a full Committee on a quarterly basis. We hold one meeting in
Northern California, one in Southern California and one in Central California. Then
meet again during Grand Lodge week. Our 1987-88 annual budget was $4,500., with
expenditures of $4,382. The 1988-89 budget is $6.560.
Major subjects and actions by the Committee for the Masonic year included:
1. Review and approval of approximately ltiO Grand Master Achievement Award
applications.
2. Approximately 22 personal Committee presentations to various Lodges in
trouble and asking for assistance.
3. Nine presentations on "How to Improve Masonic Interest and Attendance" were
given at Leadership Workshops.
4. Revised the Grand Master Achievement Award and the eligibility point system
to bring more equity to the smaller Lodges. A revised draft and cover letter dated
October 1, 1988 are enclosed for consideration and dispensing for the forthcoming
Masonic year, pending your approval.

prior to his advancement to Master, in order to encourage sound fiscal management
and planned Lodge activities.

c. Sojourners should only have to show a paid-up dues card in order to visit another
Lodge.
d We suggest the rules on how to invite non-Masons into Masonry be relaxed.
3. Change the name of Laymen's Night.
f. A financial incentive (initiation fee reduction) should be considered for past
DeMolay members to join a Masonic Lodge before their 21st to 25th birthday. This
incentive might also be expanded to other young men in the same age group category.
One of the best services our Committee provided is to meet with various Lodges
that are in trouble: and need help. As Grand Lodge representatives, we are able to show
them Grand Lodge cares. In addition, we are able to provide information from the
Leadership Workbook and other sources to assist them in meeting their planning
requirements and addressing Lodge problems. However, the size of our Committee
restricts the availability of this resource and follow-up. To help resolve this, we suggest
consideration be given to expanding the Resources Committee membership for greater
coverage. We suggest for the membership to have regional representation as per the
attached drawing. This will provide for a minimum of 12 regional members on the
Committee. Each regional representative may then have appointed 5-10 additional
members in that particular region to help meet with Lodges and for greater follow-up
action. The 12 regional representatives would continue to meet on a quarterly basis.
Regional members would also hold quarterly meetings. This pyramid effect can
provide greater representation and dissemination of information from our Resources
Committee. A minimum budget of a few hundred dollars for each region would be
anticipated to meet local expenses. A Committee expansion plan and budget will be
prepared for review if this concept meets with Grand Lodge approval.

COMMI TTEE REPORT REVIEW OF PROCEE DINGS
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A .M. of California:
In 1987-88 your Committe e reviewed some 15 publications in amity with the Grand
Lodge of California. Of these, 9 were from United States jurisdictions and 6 foreign
jurisdictions.

In presenting our annual report, we do not attempt to detail operationa l activities
of these bodies but monitor the trends within the Fraternity relating to health, strength,
growth or loss concerning the same and the. position of Freemason ry on a national and
worldwide basis.
The steady loss of membership is of great concern to all Grand Jurisdictions whose
reports we received. The loss of members is mainly due to death followed by suspension
for non-payment of dues.
There appears however, a strong effort throughout the country to "make Masonry
more visible". For example, the Grand Lodge of Pennsylvania has a Drug and Alcohol
Abuse Program. The Pennsylvania Youth Foundatio n handles a program, "How to
Master the Art of Public Speaking" on a non-profit basis, for Masonic youth groups as
well as members of the Fraternity. This can become a very effective membership
recruitmen t tool.
A prime example of zealous and dedicated Masons is revealed in an article in the
Louisiana Freemason . The Grand Master and his official family traveled to Marrero,
Louisiana to constitute Marrero Lodge No. 479, install its officers, place the building
plaque and dedicate the Lodge Hall. As far as can be determine d, no other new Lodge
had ever accomplished what was achieved by Marrero Lodge. By the time of Constitution, there were 108 charter members. This was done from 1986 to 1988 including their
Lodge which was donated by a Brother who bought the building and wanted no interest
for his investment. The Lodge will repay the Brother.
Grand Lodge of Nevada. The Grand Master noted that Nevada is a growing state
and Masonry is alive and well, and that Lodges who are taking an active part in their
communities are having a successful year. Our own Grand Master Most Worshipful
Leo B. Mark was a visiting dignitary and gave his greetin~. He admonishe d the
Brethren, particularly the Lodge Masters to check on their membersh ip to see who has
not been to Lodge for a year or more and to call them on the phone.

dependents. During the Annual Communication, one of the Distinguished Guests was
our own R : .W:.Sam M. Pavlovich, Junior Grand Warden. Membersh ip in 1986 was
9,738. In 1987 it was 9,410. Loss of3.35%.
Grand Lodge of Prince Edward Island is considerin g the use of written ritual to
help standardiz e the work. The Grand Master started a program whereby the newly

REPORT OF SPECIAL COMMI TIEE
TO EXAMINE COMMI TTEE STRUCTURE OF GRAND LODGE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. &. A. M. of California:
It has no~ been seven years since a blue ribbon commission was appointed by the
Most Worshipful Donald G. Ingalls and chaired by our distinguished Judge and
Brother Donald R. Fretz to examine the organizational structure of this Grand Lodge.
As a ~esult of that study a number of organizational changes were made which redound
to this day to the good of the Craft. Ttme, however, inevitably marches on! If
Freemasonry is to continue in its mission it must adapt to changing times.
Car~ Rowant once said: "We emphasize that we believe in change because we were

born of 1t, we have prospered and grew great by it. So the status quo has never been
our God, and we ask no one elese to bow down before it.•

It was with this philosophy in mind that your Commission on the Committe e
Stru~ure of Grand Lodge, initially appointed by Most Worshipful Jack R. Levitt, and
contmued by our Grand Master has veiwed its assignment. We are mindful too, that
~ge for change sake is not necessarily a panacea for all of the crucial issues facing
this Grand Jurisdiction and in.fact can be extremely detrimental to the fraternal health
and well-being of our beloved Masonic Fraternity.

267

PROCEEDI NGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORN IA

The ~pedal Commission almost immediately recogniz.ed that there was a need in
our volatile economy to conserve resources and at the same time broaden the par.
ticipatory base and expand services. This is a difficult task to achieve even under the
best of circumstances; but particularly difficult in a time when we are experiencing
radical s~ in the economic pendulum and a membership which is advancing in age
and decreasing in numbers.

We recommend that the Jurisprudenc e Committee consist of no more than five
bcrs and that the Policy and General Purposes Committee consists of no more
=seven members which is sufficient to provide for a diversification of opinion and
p«!lllpl consideratio n of all points of view within the 180 day time frame for the review
iod distribution of proposed legislation.

266

It is es.sential in the view of this commission that we broaden the base, that we bring
to our Grand Lodge organization al structure the brightest, the youngest, the most
innovative men and ideas our Brethren can offer. We are also aware that we must
curtail expenses wherever possible. Accordingly, this commission recommends that
the following steps be considered to achieve the goals and objectives heretofore stated:

1. We recommend that the following committtees of Grand Lodge be continued
as mandated in the Constitution and Ordinances:
k. Recognition of Foreign Grand Lodges
a. Fmance
l. Library and Museum
b. Investment
m.Retiremen t Pension Plan
c. Trial Review
n Commercialism
d. Memorial Service
o. Charitable Gifts
e. Masonic Code
p. Special Gifts
f. Review of Proceedings
q. Taxation
g. Credentials
r. Insurance
h Grand Lodge Week Activities
s. Charters
i . Temple Properties
j. Masonic Service Bureaus
We recommend that the following committees be consolidated and restructured:
b. Lodge Resource Developmen t
a. Masonic Education
c. Masonic Leadership Workshop
as the " Committee On Masonic EducatJon And Leadership Development ••
a. Old Masonic Temple at Los Angeles b. Quitman Temple
d . Cemeteries
c. Columbia Temple
as the " CommJttee On Masonic History And Historical Places "
b. U.S. Constitution Observance
a. Public Schools
d. Films and Creative Projects
c. Masonic Public Relations
e. Public Information
as the " Committee On Public Observation Programs And Public Relations ".
b. Sojourners
a. Youth
c. Masonic Widows Program
as the " Committee on Masonk Membership Services and Developmen t•.
We recommend that the membership of these two newly restructured committees
be greatly expanded with committees appointed by the Grand Master at the District
and Division level to coordinate the public observance programs and Masonic services
and development activities of this Grand Lodge on a continuing and uniform basis.

We recommend that the Committee on By-Laws be eliminated and that it's
fuDCtions and responsibilities be handled administratively through the office of the
Grand Secretary.
We recommend in the interest of the Grand Master's responsibilities for the
overall superintende nce of the Craft; that the office of Grand Lecturer be made an
appaintive office of the Grand Lodge and the Brother so appointed to that position,
shall serve at the will and pleasure of the Grand Master. This recommenda tion is made
bceaUSO the Grand Lecturer is the only committee chairman in the Grand Lodge who
is accorded the privilege of election.
We recommend that the Committee on Travel Allowance and Pay of Members be
eliminated and that the Grand Secretary's office, with the approval of the Fmance
Committee and pursuant to that section of the California Masonic Code governing pay
ofmembers from the State of Hawaii reimburse Hawaiian delegates only in accordance
with the formula specified in the Code. The commission makes this recommenda tion
because it has learned and beleives that some of those Constituent Lodges entitled to
reimbursement do not pick up their checks as required at the conclusion of the Grand
Lodge and others do not negotiate the checks picked up in a timely manner, thereby
creating bookkeeping and administrative problems for many months after the Annual
Communication. The fiscal impact of partially eliminating this particular expense will
have a salutary effect on the per capita tax which will far outweigh the subsidy to
delegates who, if they liad to depend on such subsides, would be unable to attend the
Annual Communication.
Your commission recommends that all references and statutory requirement s
mandating a minimum number of personnel on the several committees be eliminated
and that the staffmg of said committees be left to the sound discretion and wise
judgement of the Grand Master. The commission believes that the staffing requirements of many of the committees change from year to year and that the composition
thereof should be dictated by the needs of the Grand Master in executing bis program
or by the requirement s of the California Masonic Code on those committees whose
structure has not been altered by the recommenda tions of this, or any other previous
report.
Your commission recommends that all committees report in writing quarterly to
the Grand Master and that said reports be directed to the Grand Committee Coordinator in the office of the Grand Secretary. The chairman of the commission, in
discussing this matter with the Grand Secretary bas learned that coordination and
compilation of committee reports can be accomplished by the Grand Secretary's office
without overloading bis very efficient and effective staff or retaining additional personnel. The importance of obtaining reports from the several committees cannot be
ovcrempasized and experience has found that even the most effective and dedicated
committee chairman need periodic follow-up reminders of deadlines. The Grand
Lodge Committee Coordinator s responsiblity amoung others would be to summarize
reports and refer them to the Executive Committee and others for reveiw and implementation.

268

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

Your commission recommends that non-members of Grand Lodge be permitted
to serve on Grand Lodge Committees as full-fledged members and that a special
credential be developed to entitle them to the privileges of the floor at Grand Lodge
and to participate in all proceedings except voting. We recommend however, that not
more than one third of the compsition of such committees be composed of non-members of Grand Lodge and that in every instance the chairman of the committee be a
member of Grand Lodge.
We recommend that a special commission be chartered by the Grand Master to
explore the feasibility of instituting a system of District Deputy Grand Masters to assist
the Grand Master in the discharge of his awesome executive and administrative
responsibilities.
Your commission recommends to the Grand Master that he carefully consider the
feasibility of recommending that the uniform code of by-Laws be amended to provide
for an Executive Committee in each of the constituent Lodges, consisting of the Master,
Wardens and immediate Past Master of the Lodge to be appointed at the first Stated
meeting immediately following the annual Installation of Officers. The executive
committtee of the several constituent Lodges shall oversee and develop plans to
provide for the observance of all official Grand Lodge Public Observances and
Programs and it will be the responsibility of said committee to report on a quarterly
basis to the Grand Lodge Committee Coordinator or to the District Inspector as to
the activities of said committee in carrying out the responsibilities delegated to it.
Nothing herein provided shall overrule the primacy of each Lodge to direct the
Executive Committee in carrying out the individual mission of each Lodge; nor are the
duties and responsibilities of the Worshipful Master with respect to the Ancient
Landmarks, Constitution and Ordinances abrogated herein in any manner.
Your special Commission has had as its sole objective the goal of assisting the Most
Worshipful Grand Master to carry out his arduous mission with efficiency and dispatch. The function of our Grand Lodge and its Grand Master when the Grand lodge
is in recess is to superintend the Craft, to carry out the mission of Freemasonry and
advance and promote our cause. Accordingly, we believe that this is best accomplished
when committees of Grand Lodge are formulated to help the Constiuent Lodges to
uniformly carry out a program which demonstrates the strength and stability of the
Craft throughout the Grand Jurisdiction of California and Hawaii and when Brethren
work with each other in unity and concord.
Your commission is grateful to the several committee chairmen who contributed
their wisdom, expertise, and cooperation to the preparation of this report.
We are appreciative of the opportunity to be of service to the Grand Lodge. We
thank Most Worshipful Grand Master Leo B. Marie, Past Grand Master Jack R. Levitt
and Very Worshipful Grand Secretary, Robert A. Klinger for their assistance.
Respectfully submitted,
John W. Driskell, P.G.M., Chariman

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON TAXATION
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of Califomia:
The objective of this Committee is to render advice on matters of taxation when
requested by the Grand Lodge, subordinate Lodges and other organizations under
their jurisdiction, with respect to matters of income, property, sales and employment

taJCS·
Our goals, as tax practitioners, are to:
1. Review current developments in taxation applicable to the Fraternity, and
recommend or inform others of actions appropriate to changes in tax law, regulations
or court decisions;
2. Respond promptly and professionally to requests for tax advice made of the
Committee; also, represent Lodges and Temple Associations before the Internal
Revenue Service and/or Franchise Tax Board;
3. Prepare a report for publication in the annual Proceedings of the Grand Lodge
00 matters of current interest in taxation of interest to our Fraternity.

During the past Masonic year, our assistance was requested on a variety of tax
matters regarding income, property, sales and employment taxes. Each year a member
of this Committee updates instructions for filing tax forms due from subordinate
organizations during the year to various government entities. The Grand Secretary
sends a copy to the Secretary of each such organization.
More members are needed on this Committee who have the qualifications of
C.PA. or tax. attorney. Perhaps each District Inspector might be requested to furnish
the names of candidat~s with such qualifications.
Resolutions reviewed by the Committee for comment on possible tax consequences included Nos. 88-19, 88-21, 88-33 and 87-23., as referred by the Grand Master. To
understand possible consequences it is important to review how Lodges are taxed.
Masonic Lodges are exempt from Federal and California income taxes, regardless
of the amount of income from dues, interest or dividends, with certain exceptions. A
Lodges is taxed on income from a trade or business which is unrelated to the fraternal
purposes of the Lodge. When exempt organizations compete with tax-paying businesses, "unrelated business income" from competitive activity is taxed to remove any
economic advantage which exempt status might confer. Such unrelated business
income is a taxable trade or business activity. For example, operating a restaurant
constitutes a trade or business; holding periodic dinners does not qualify as a trade or
business. Income from events conducted by tax-exempt fraternal organizations is not
taxable if substantially all the labor required to bold the event is performed for the
Lodge without compensation.
California sales and use tax consequences attach to certain Lodge events. Sales

tax is assessed upon the sale of tangible personal property, such as meals or merchandise at garage sales even if labeled as "donation".
Exemption from sales and use tax is available to Lodges for receipts from furnish-

ing meals if the meals are furnished: (1) exclusively to members and (2) less frequently
than once a week. If the Lodge furnishes meals to non-members, then all receipts from

270

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

meals are subject to tax, whether furnished to members or non-members. However,
meals paid for by members are considered furnished to members and therefore not
subject to tax even though consumed by guests who are not members. Tickets for
non-members who attend Lodge dinners should be purchased by members; the Lodge
need not concern itself whether the member is reimbursed by the guest.

We are most grateful to our Grand Master Most Worshipful Leo B. Mark for the
nerous assistance and counsel which he gave whenever called upon, and to Stanley
Channon, Deputy Grand Master, Sam M. Pavlovich, Senior Grand Warden and
Ronald A. Sherod, Junior Grand Warden, for the fraternal support they were always
ready to give, whenever called upon.

If a Lodge is subject to sales tax, it must apply for a California Seller's permit,
obtainable from a local office of the State Board of Equalizaiton.
Committee recommendations concerning the four Resolutions referred to it are
based on our understanding of the tax issues of each Resolution, separately explained.

Our Grand Secretary, Robert A. Klinger and Assistant Grand Secretary, H.
Francis Lewis, have always made the time to answer questions, and give good counsel
to this Committee, when problems arose. For this, we owe them a debt of gratitude
which can never be fully repaid. It has always been a comfort to realize that they were
there, and that the advice they gave was sound.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON TEMPLE PROPERTIES
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of California:
The Committee on Temple Properties is pleased to submit this annual report of
its activities for the 1987-88 Masonic year.

During the past year many projects of refurbishing, altering and improving Temple
Buildin~ were undertaken. Most were passed by this Committee without difficulty,
the members of the Temple Associations having given this Committee a complete
package of the work to be done, and financial statements showing how the projects
were to be financed without imposing a hardship on the Temple Association, or the
Lodge(s) which owns and controls the Association. We appreciate the cooperation
given us by those Temple Associations which send us all the details we need in order
to come to a well informed and justifiable decision regarding which they hope to
undertake for the improvement of their properties, physically and financially.
The Form 200, Profit and Loss, and Fmancial Statements seem to be coming into
this office in greater numbers this year than they did last. However, we find that there
are still too many Temple Associations which are disregarding the mandate in the
second paragraph of Section 1208 of the California Masonic Code, regarding the
submitting of a Profit and Loss, and Financial Statement (Form 200), at the close of
their fiscal year. The forms are sent to each Temple Associaton at the beginning of
each calendar year.
Many of the Temple Associations have adopted the Uniform Articles of Incor·
poration and the Uniform Code of By-Laws mandated by Grand Lodge for all Temple
Associations in its Jurisdiction. Those Temple Associations which have not yet done
so are urged to request copies of the Articles and Code from this Committee, adopt
them as soon as possible, and inform this Committee of their action.
Several of our Committeemen have been invited during the past year, to visit
Lodges or Temple Associations, and speak to, or advise, the members of the respective
organizations regarding the establishment or management of Temple Associations.
This Committee is most happy to reply to such requests, and to assist as best it can in
the solution of problems which have arisen and procedures which may avoid future
problems.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON TRAVEL ALLOWANCES

Those entitled to travel allowances are the Master, or in his absence, the ranking
Warden, or in the absence of the Master and Wardens, the duly Elected Representative
in accordance with Section 1148 of the California Masonic Code. However, no payment
shall be allowed for the Officers or Representatives of any Lodge, the dues of which
have not been paid in full, or which shall be reported by the Grand Secretary as having
been delinquent in the transmission of Certificates of Election and Installation of
Officers of their respective Lodges.
Past Grand Masters not on Committees, will be reimbursed as provided in Section
1150 of the California Masonic Code.
In accordance with Section 1148 of the California Masonic Code, when a Master
and Warden from the same Lodge are present at a Communication, and one of said
Officers serves on a Grand Lodge Committee entitled to travel and expense reimbursement, he shall be reimbursed under Section 1150 of the California Masonic Code.
The other Officer shaU receive reimbursement under Section 1148 of the California
Masonic Code, as the Officer representing his Lodge on the floor of Grand Lodge.

Mileage from the various points within the state of California to San Francisco has
been taken from the published records of the California State Automobile Association.
Mileage from points in the state of Hawaii to San Francisco, has been taken from the
published reports of Airlines in accordance with Section 1148 of the California
Masonic Code. No compensation is allowed to members representing Lodges in San
Francisco and the immediate 30 mile vicinity. Compensation to members from the state
of California has been computed on the basis of eleven (11) cents per mile, the rate
fixed by the Committee on F"mance. Compensation to members from the state of
Hawaii has been computed on the basis of regularly scheduled major Airlines, from
Honolulu to San Francisco, plus inter-island air fare to Honolulu when necessary.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON YOUTH ORDERS
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.&A.M. of California:
The functions of the Committee on Youth Orders continue to be two-fold. The
first and primary function is to make ourselves known to and get acquainted with the
individual Lodges in this jurisdiction, to encourage them to initiate programs and to
expand their activities in support of our Masonic Youth Groups and to take a ~ore
personal interest in their activities. Secondly, it is our express purpose to get acquamtcd
with the youth groups themselves and with their adult leaders, to let them know of our
interest in their well-being, to make their programs and activities known to the Lodge:&
and to support and assist them in every possible way.

L Channon. Re-appointed to serve as Memorial Temple Trustees were Robert 0.

California, a nonprofit, public benefit corporation, as of June 30, 1988
and 1987, and the related statements of support, revenue and expenses
and changes in fund balances for the years then ended. Our examinations
were made in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards and,

circumstances.

fairly the financial position of The Masonic Homes of California at June
30, 1988 and 1987 and the results of its operations and changes in fund
balances for the years then ended, in conformity with generally accepted
